edges.description: Blockage, host reaction and lymphatic dysfunction caused by adult worms eventually result in lymphedema.
Applies to bancroftian filariasis (edges cannot carry a subtype); lymphatics of the male genitalia are frequently affected, leading to hydrocele.
Recurrent episodes of secondary skin infection in the affected limb present as ADLA, a form of cellulitis.
Repeated, prolonged infection can progress lymphedema to elephantiasis, a buildup of excess tissue in the affected area.

evidence.snippet: the World Health Organization recommended treatments for lymphatic filariasis include the use of Albendazole (400mg) twice per year in co-endemic areas with loa loa, Ivermectin (200mcg/kg) in combination with Albendazole (400mg) in areas that are co-endemic with onchocerciasis, ivermectin (200mcg/kg) with diethylcarbamazine citrate (DEC) (6mg/kg) and albendazole (400mg) in areas without onchocerciasis.
